By leveraging this approach, it is possible to achieve the desired depth, width, morphology, and detail of a sufficient weld, thereby producing full-density parts with minimal to no porosity or voids. The key advantage of single weld tracks lies in their ability to penetrate 2–3-layer thicknesses deep while maintaining an accommodating width that prevents lack of fusion between adjacent passes. Recognizing the importance of standardization in metal AM, ASTM International, SAE, and other national and international technical committees, along with academia, have invested UNCLASSIFIED AMMT – 316H SS Los Alamos National Laboratory Page 1-6 significant efforts in developing a qualification process for metal AM machines and parts. The ASTM F42 subcommittee has been at the forefront of this initiative, focusing on developing standards for the AM qualification process over the past several years. A major milestone was achieved in April 2020 with the release of ASTM F3434-20, a guide for additive manufacturing – installation/operation and performance qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) of laser-beam powder bed fusion equipment for production manufacturing. Additionally, the Aerospace Industries Association (AIA) AM Working Group published the "Recommended Guidance for Certification of AM Components" report in February 2020. This section reviews these guidelines and recommendations, along with others found in literature and the AMMT work packages. It is noteworthy that most of these considerations were developed with aerospace parts in mind. For detailed information about certification requirements and recommendations, readers are directed to references 28-32.
